subject: maths
title: Decimals and Percentages
seo_title: Year 5 Decimals and Percentages Worksheets: Thousandths, Rounding and Per Cent
standard_text: Read and write decimal numbers as fractions [for example, 0.71 = 71/100]; recognise and use thousandths and relate them to tenths, hundredths and decimal equivalents; round decimals with two decimal places to the nearest whole number and to one decimal place; read, write, order and compare numbers with up to three decimal places; recognise the per cent symbol (%) and understand that per cent relates to ‘number of parts per hundred’, and write percentages as a fraction with denominator 100, and as a decimal; solve problems which require knowing percentage and decimal equivalents of 1/2, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5, 4/5 and those fractions with a denominator of a multiple of 10 or 25.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 decimals and percentages worksheets for the National Curriculum: decimals as fractions, thousandths, comparing and ordering up to three decimal places, rounding to the nearest whole number and 1 decimal place, and per cent as parts per hundred. 100 maths questions with an answer key.
key_big: Per cent means parts per hundred: 37% = 37/100 = 0.37. Three decimal places are thousandths: 0.007 = 7/1000.
key_sub: Compare decimals by giving them the same number of places: 0.5 = 0.500 > 0.45. Round with the next digit: 3.45 rounds up to 3.5. Know 1/2 = 50%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%, 2/5 = 40%, 4/5 = 80%.
body_html:
Decimals as fractions

The number of decimal places tells you the denominator. One place is tenths, two places are hundredths, three places are thousandths.

DecimalFractionSaid as
0.77107 tenths
0.717110071 hundredths
0.007710007 thousandths
0.4534531000453 thousandths

Comparing and ordering

Give the numbers the same number of decimal places by adding zeros at the end. Then compare the digits from the left: ones, tenths, hundredths, thousandths.

Example

Order 0.5, 0.45 and 0.405 from smallest to greatest.

Write 0.500, 0.450 and 0.405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths.

Answer: 0.405, 0.45, 0.5

Rounding decimals

To the nearest whole number, look at the tenths digit. To 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit. 5 or more: round up. 4 or less: round down.

Example

Round 5.96 to 1 decimal place.

The hundredths digit is 6, so round up. 9 tenths + 1 tenth = 10 tenths = 1 whole.

Answer: 6.0

Per cent

Per cent (%) means parts per hundred. 37% = 37100 = 0.37.

To change a fraction into a percentage, make the denominator 100 first.

FractionHundredthsDecimalPercentage
12501000.550%
14251000.2525%
15201000.220%
25401000.440%

310301000.330%
Test score

Freya scores 18 out of 25. What percentage is that?

25 × 4 = 100, so multiply the top by 4 too: 1825 = 72100.

Answer: 72%

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.45 > 0.5 because it is longerUse the same places: 0.45 < 0.50
0.007 = 7100Three places means thousandths: 71000
Rounding 3.45 to 3.4Halfway rounds up: 3.5
15 = 15% or 0.515 = 20100 = 0.2 = 20%
0.4 = 4%0.4 = 0.40 = 40%

faq.q: What do children learn about decimals and percentages in Year 5?
faq.a: In Year 5 children write decimals as fractions (0.71 = 71/100), learn thousandths, compare and order numbers with up to three decimal places, round decimals to the nearest whole number and to one decimal place, and learn that per cent means parts per hundred.

faq.q: How do you explain thousandths to a child?
faq.a: Split 1 hundredth into 10 equal parts: each part is 1 thousandth, written 0.001. Thousandths are the third place after the decimal point, so 0.007 = 7/1000.

faq.q: How do you compare decimals with different numbers of digits?
faq.a: Add zeros at the end so they have the same number of decimal places, then compare from the left. 0.5 = 0.500 and 0.45 = 0.450, so 0.5 is greater even though 0.45 has more digits.

faq.q: Which fraction, decimal and percentage facts should Year 5 know?
faq.a: 1/2 = 0.5 = 50%, 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%, 1/5 = 0.2 = 20%, 2/5 = 0.4 = 40% and 4/5 = 0.8 = 80%. For tenths, twentieths, twenty-fifths and fiftieths, make the denominator 100 to find the percentage.

items.q: Write 0.3 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.3 has one decimal place, so the 3 is in the tenths place: 3 tenths = 310.

items.q: Write 0.71 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.71 has two decimal places, so the last digit is in the hundredths place: 71 hundredths = 71100. 7110 would be 7.1.

items.q: Write 0.09 as a fraction.
items.e: Two decimal places means hundredths. The tenths digit is 0, so 0.09 = 9 hundredths = 9100.

items.q: Write 29100 as a decimal.
items.e: 29 hundredths: the last digit goes in the second place after the point. 29100 = 0.29.

items.q: Write 0.007 as a fraction.
items.e: 0.007 has three decimal places, so the 7 is in the thousandths place: 71000. 7100 would be 0.07.

items.q: Write 71000 as a decimal.
items.e: 7 thousandths: the 7 goes in the third place after the point. Write 0s in the tenths and hundredths places: 0.007. 0.07 is 7 hundredths.

items.q: Write 0.453 as a fraction.
items.e: Three decimal places means thousandths: 0.453 = 453 thousandths = 4531000. 31000 is only the last digit.

items.q: Write 631000 as a decimal.
items.e: 63 thousandths = 6 hundredths and 3 thousandths. The last digit must be in the third place: 0.063. 0.63 would be 63 hundredths.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 2.738?
items.e: The red 8 is the third digit after the decimal point, in the thousandths column. Its value is 8 thousandths = 0.008.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 5.064?
items.e: The red 6 is the second digit after the decimal point, in the hundredths column. Its value is 6 hundredths = 0.06. The 0 holds the tenths place.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 3.124?
items.e: Tenths, hundredths, thousandths: 3 . 1 2 4. The 4 is in the thousandths place, so it is worth 4 thousandths = 0.004.

items.q: Write 3 ones, 5 hundredths and 2 thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: There are 0 tenths, so write a 0 in the tenths place: 3 . 0 5 2 = 3.052. 3.52 would have 5 tenths.

items.q: Which number is equal to 0.6?
items.e: A 0 at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 0.6 = 0.60 = 0.600. 0.06 and 0.006 have the 6 in a different place.

items.q: 1 hundredth is split into 10 equal parts. What decimal is each part?
items.e: A hundredth divided by 10 is a thousandth: 11000 = 0.001. 1 whole = 10 tenths = 100 hundredths = 1,000 thousandths.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 1 hundredth?
items.e: 1 hundredth = 0.01 = 0.010. That is 10 thousandths.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0.3?
items.e: 1 tenth = 100 thousandths, so 3 tenths = 300 thousandths. 0.3 = 0.300 = 3001000.

items.q: 610 + 4100 + 91000 = ?
items.e: 6 tenths, 4 hundredths and 9 thousandths: 0 . 6 4 9 = 0.649.

items.q: 0.35 = 35100 = ?1000
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 10: 35100 = 3501000. So the missing number is 350. 0.35 = 0.350.

items.q: Write 2.09 as a mixed number.
items.e: 2 wholes, then 0.09 = 9 hundredths. So 2.09 = 2 9100. 2 910 would be 2.9.

items.q: What number is 1 thousandth more than 4.209?
items.e: 9 thousandths + 1 thousandth = 10 thousandths = 1 hundredth. So 4.209 + 0.001 = 4.210 = 4.21. 4.219 adds 1 hundredth, not 1 thousandth.

sets.title: Compare and order decimals up to 3 places

items.q: Compare 0.5 and 0.45.
items.e: 0.5 = 0.50. Compare the tenths: 5 tenths > 4 tenths. So 0.5 > 0.45. More digits does not mean a bigger number.

items.q: Compare 0.38 and 0.4.
items.e: 0.4 = 0.40. Compare the tenths: 3 < 4. So 0.38 < 0.4.

items.q: Compare 2.07 and 2.070.
items.e: A 0 at the end does not change the value. 2.07 = 2.070, so 2.07 = 2.070.

items.q: Compare 0.009 and 0.09.
items.e: 0.09 = 0.090. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 9. So 0.009 < 0.09. 9 thousandths is less than 9 hundredths.

items.q: Compare 0.405 and 0.45.
items.e: Write both with 3 places: 0.405 and 0.450. The tenths are the same. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 5. So 0.405 < 0.45.

items.q: Compare 3.125 and 3.12.
items.e: 3.12 = 3.120. Ones, tenths and hundredths are the same. Compare the thousandths: 5 > 0. So 3.125 > 3.12.

items.q: Compare 1.9 and 1.899.
items.e: 1.9 = 1.900. The ones are the same. Compare the tenths: 9 > 8. So 1.9 > 1.899.

items.q: Compare 0.62 and 0.602.
items.e: 0.62 = 0.620. The tenths are the same. Compare the hundredths: 2 > 0. So 0.62 > 0.602.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.700, 0.680, 0.699, 0.075. Compare the tenths first: only 0.7 has 7 tenths. So 0.7 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.205, 0.250, 0.300, 0.520. The smallest is 0.205, even though it has the most digits.

items.q: Which number is between 0.4 and 0.5?
items.e: 0.4 = 0.400 and 0.5 = 0.500. 0.408 is between them. 0.048 and 0.399 are less than 0.4, and 0.54 is more than 0.5.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: The line goes from 1.2 to 1.3 in 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 hundredth. Count 4 spaces on from 1.20: 1.24.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
0.5, 0.45, 0.405
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.500, 0.450, 0.405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths. So 0.405, 0.45, 0.5.

items.q: What number is 0.01 less than 3.2?
items.e: 3.2 = 3.20. Take away 1 hundredth: exchange 1 tenth for 10 hundredths. 3.20 − 0.01 = 3.19. 3.199 is 0.001 less.

items.q:
Order from greatest to smallest:
3.2, 3.18, 3.205, 3.02
Which number is between 2.3 and 2.31?
What number is at the red dot?
items.e: The line goes from 0.32 to 0.33 in 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1 thousandth. Count 6 spaces on from 0.320: 0.326.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
0.6, 0.06, 0.606, 0.066
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0.600, 0.060, 0.606, 0.066. Compare 600, 60, 606 and 66 thousandths. So 0.06, 0.066, 0.6, 0.606.

items.q:
How many of these numbers are greater than 0.6?
0.59, 0.61, 0.596, 0.601

0.4□7 < 0.45
What is the greatest digit that can go in the box?
items.e: 0.45 = 0.450. With 4 in the box: 0.447 < 0.450. With 5: 0.457 > 0.450. So the greatest digit is 4.

sets.title: Round decimals to the nearest whole number and to 1 decimal place

items.q: Round 4.38 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: To round to the nearest whole number, look at the tenths digit: 3. 4 or less rounds down. 4.38 is between 4 and 5, nearer to 4.

items.q: Round 7.62 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Look at the tenths digit: 6. 5 or more rounds up. 7.62 is between 7 and 8, nearer to 8.

items.q: Round 0.83 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Look at the tenths digit: 8. 5 or more rounds up. 0.83 is between 0 and 1, nearer to 1.

items.q: Round 9.51 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Look at the tenths digit: 5. 5 or more rounds up. 9.51 is between 9 and 10, so it rounds to 10.

items.q: The red dot shows 8.36. Round 8.36 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: The dot is between 8 and 9. It is before the halfway mark (8.5), so it is nearer to 8. The tenths digit is 3: 4 or less rounds down.

items.q: Round 6.72 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: To round to 1 decimal place, look at the hundredths digit: 2. 4 or less rounds down. 6.72 is between 6.7 and 6.8, nearer to 6.7.

items.q: Round 0.64 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: Look at the hundredths digit: 4. 4 or less rounds down. 0.64 is between 0.6 and 0.7, nearer to 0.6.

items.q: Round 2.08 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: 2.08 is between 2.0 and 2.1. Look at the hundredths digit: 8. 5 or more rounds up, so the 0 tenths become 1 tenth: 2.1.

items.q: The red dot shows 3.47. Round 3.47 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: The dot is between 3.4 and 3.5. It is past the halfway mark (3.45), so it is nearer to 3.5. The hundredths digit is 7: 5 or more rounds up.

items.q: Round 12.49 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Look only at the tenths digit: 4. 4 or less rounds down, so 12.49 rounds to 12. Do not round twice (12.49 → 12.5 → 13): 12.49 is less than halfway (12.5).

items.q: Round 3.45 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more rounds up. 3.45 is exactly halfway between 3.4 and 3.5, and halfway rounds up: 3.5.

items.q: Round 14.35 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: Look at the hundredths digit: 5. 5 or more rounds up. 14.35 is halfway between 14.3 and 14.4, so it rounds up to 14.4.

items.q: Round 2.45 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: Look only at the tenths digit: 4. 4 or less rounds down, so 2.45 rounds to 2. Rounding twice (2.45 → 2.5 → 3) is a common mistake.

items.q: Round 5.96 to 1 decimal place.
items.e: Look at the hundredths digit: 6, so round up. 9 tenths + 1 tenth = 10 tenths = 1 whole. So 5.96 rounds to 6.0. Keep the 0 to show it is rounded to 1 decimal place.

items.q: Which number rounds to 4.3 to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Look at the hundredths digit. 4.26 rounds up to 4.3. 4.36 rounds to 4.4, 4.23 rounds to 4.2, and 4.35 is halfway, so it rounds up to 4.4.

items.q: Which number rounds to 7 to the nearest whole number?
items.e: 6.52 has 5 tenths, so it rounds up to 7. 7.5 and 7.61 round up to 8. 6.49 has 4 tenths, so it rounds down to 6.

items.q: What is the smallest number with 2 decimal places that rounds to 5.4?
items.e: Numbers from 5.35 up to 5.44 round to 5.4. The smallest is 5.35, because halfway rounds up. 5.45 rounds up to 5.5.

items.q: What is the greatest number with 2 decimal places that rounds to 2 to the nearest whole number?
items.e: Numbers up to 2.49 round down to 2. 2.49 is the greatest. 2.5 is halfway, so it rounds up to 3.

items.q: A number rounds to 6 to the nearest whole number and to 5.8 to 1 decimal place. Which number could it be?
items.e: 5.76 rounds to 5.8 (6 hundredths: round up) and to 6 (7 tenths: round up). So 5.76. 5.74 rounds to 5.7, 5.86 rounds to 5.9, and 6.8 rounds to 7.

items.q: Round 4.65 to the nearest whole number and to 1 decimal place.
items.e: Nearest whole number: the tenths digit is 6, so round up to 5. 1 decimal place: the hundredths digit is 5, so round up to 4.7. Answer: 5 and 4.7.

sets.title: Per cent: parts per hundred, fractions and decimals

items.q: What does per cent mean?
items.e: “Per cent” means out of 100 (parts per hundred). 23% means 23 parts out of 100.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 37 of the 100 squares are shaded. Per cent means parts per hundred, so it is 37%. 63% is the white part.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 6 full columns of 10 are shaded: 60 of the 100 squares = 60%. 6% would be only 6 small squares.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 8 of the 100 squares are shaded: 8%. 80% would be 8 full columns.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is not shaded?
items.e: 45 squares are shaded, so 100 − 45 = 55 squares are white. 55 out of 100 = 55%.

items.q: Which shows the shaded part as a fraction and as a percentage?
items.e: 25 of 100 squares: 25100 = 25%. The denominator is 100 because the square has 100 parts.

items.q: Write 23% as a fraction.
items.e: Per cent means out of 100: 23% = 23100.

items.q: Write 9% as a fraction.
items.e: 9% = 9 out of 100 = 9100. 910 would be 90%.

items.q: Write 71100 as a percentage.
items.e: 71100 means 71 out of 100, so it is 71%.

items.q: Write 310 as a percentage.
items.e: Make the denominator 100: 310 = 30100 = 30%. 3% would be 3100.

items.q: Write 45% as a decimal.
items.e: 45% = 45100 = 45 hundredths = 0.45.

items.q: Write 6% as a decimal.
items.e: 6% = 6100 = 6 hundredths. Hundredths are the second place after the point: 0.06. 0.6 is 60%.

items.q: Write 0.4 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 40 hundredths = 40100 = 40%. 4% would be 0.04.

items.q: Write 0.83 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.83 = 83 hundredths = 83100 = 83%.

items.q: Write 90% as a decimal.
items.e: 90% = 90100 = 910 = 0.9. 0.09 is only 9%.

items.q: Write 0.05 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.05 = 5 hundredths = 5100 = 5%. 50% would be 0.5.

items.q: 100% of something is …
items.e: 100% = 100100 = 1. So 100% is the whole amount. 1% is one hundredth of it.

items.q: 64% of the pupils in a school have a pet. What percentage do not have a pet?
Which of these is not equal to 710?
items.e: 710 = 70100 = 0.7 = 70%. 7% is 7100, which is much smaller.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all as hundredths: 0.5 = 50%, 48%, 0.45 = 45%, 5%. The greatest is 0.5.

items.q: Write 12 as a percentage.
items.e: 12 = 50100 = 50%. Do not just write the digits 1 and 2.

items.q: Write 14 as a decimal.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 0.25. 0.4 uses the 4 from the denominator.

items.q: Write 15 as a percentage.
items.e: 5 × 20 = 100, so 15 = 20100 = 20%. 15% writes the digits, and 50% confuses 15 with 12.

items.q: Write 25 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 = 410 = 0.4. 0.2 is only 15.

items.q: Write 45 as a percentage.
items.e: 15 = 20%, so 45 = 4 × 20% = 80%. 20% is the part that is left.

items.q: Kai scores 18 out of 25 in a spelling test. What percentage does he score?
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 1825 = 72100 = 72%. 7% uses the 7 marks he got wrong.

items.q: Write 325 as a percentage.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 325 = 12100 = 12%. 75% comes from 3 × 25.

items.q: Write 1320 as a percentage.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 1320 = 65100 = 65%. Multiply the numerator by 5 too.

items.q: Write 750 as a decimal.
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so 750 = 14100 = 0.14. 0.07 forgets to double the numerator.

items.q: Which is greater: 35 or 55%?
items.e: 35 = 60100 = 60%. 60% > 55%, so 35 is greater.

items.q: A pencil costs 45p. What percentage of £1 is that?
items.e: £1 = 100p. 45p out of 100p = 45100 = 45%.

items.q: Which is smaller: 15 or 0.15?
items.e: 15 = 210 = 0.2 = 0.20. 0.15 < 0.20, so 0.15 is smaller. 15 is not 0.15.

items.q: Grace’s tablet battery has 0.35 of a full charge left. What percentage is that?
items.e: 0.35 = 35 hundredths = 35100 = 35%. 65% of the charge has been used.

items.q: 40% of the pupils in a class are boys. What fraction of the class are girls?
items.e: 100% − 40% = 60% are girls. 60% = 60100 = 35. 25 is the boys.

items.q: A jumper is 15 off in one shop and 25% off in another shop. Which shop takes off more?
c: the 15 off shop
items.e: 15 = 20%, and 25% > 20%. So the 25% off shop takes off more.

items.q: A jug holds 1 litre. Oliver pours 0.6 litres of water into it. What percentage of the jug is full?
items.e: 0.6 = 610 = 60100 = 60%. 40% is the empty part.

items.q: Amelia has done 0.8 of her homework. Freya has done 75% of her homework. Who has done more?
items.e: 0.8 = 80%. 80% > 75%, so Amelia has done more.

items.q: There are 50 pupils in Year 5. 19 of them have school dinners. What percentage have school dinners?
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so 1950 = 38100 = 38%. 62% is the pupils who do not have school dinners.

items.q: In a maths test out of 25, Isla scores 22. Harry scores 90%. Who has the higher score?
items.e: 2225 = 88100 = 88%. 90% > 88%, so Harry has the higher score.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
35, 0.55, 58%
items.e: As hundredths: 35 = 0.60, 0.55 and 58% = 0.58. So 0.55, 58%, 35.
